record.paper_title: Geodesic Nets: Some Examples and Open Problems
record.original_question: In the finite sevenfold star construction G_n(phi), with layers V_0 through V_n and suspension-angle functions phi_0(phi), phi_1(phi), ..., phi_n(phi) defined from the one-hook and two-hook suspension geometry, is it true that for sufficiently small nonzero phi the finite sequence phi_0(phi), phi_1(phi), ..., phi_n(phi) has no repeated value? If so, does the non-overlap criterion imply that G_n(phi) is a geodesic net rather than merely a geodesic multinet, with every edge having weight one, exactly 14 unbalanced vertices, and arbitrarily many balanced vertices as n is chosen large?

evidence.quote: Lemma 4.5.5. If for any fixed ϕ ∈ (−ϵ, ϵ), the sequence ϕi(ϕ) never repeats itself, all edges of the resulting geodesic net Gn(ϕ) intersect transversally (if at all). In other words, there are no edges with weight other than one.

Conjecture 4.5.8. For small nonzero ϕ ∈ (−ϵ, ϵ), the sequence ϕi (ϕ) never repeats itself. This implies that Gn (ϕ) is a geodesic net for which all edges have weight one. So this Gn (ϕ) would in fact fulfill all required conditions: (a) There are 14 unbalanced vertices. (b) For n large enough, we can achieve an arbitrarily large number of balanced vertices. (c) All edges have weight one.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following "finite sevenfold star" construction in the Euclidean plane. For a small real parameter ϕ in some interval (−ε, ε), one builds a planar graph G_n(ϕ) organized into n+1 layers V_0, V_1, …, V_n of vertices, obtained inductively by attaching to each existing "hook" vertex either a one-hook or two-hook suspension that emanates from it along geodesic (straight) segments. Each layer V_i carries an associated "suspension-angle" function ϕ_i(ϕ), defined as the angle that the corresponding suspension edge in V_i makes with a fixed reference direction; ϕ_0(ϕ), ϕ_1(ϕ), …, ϕ_n(ϕ) are real-analytic functions of ϕ with ϕ_i(0) = 0.

A geodesic net is a finite graph embedded in the plane whose edges are straight segments, in which every interior ("balanced") vertex has the property that the sum of the unit tangent vectors of the edges incident to it is zero, and where each edge has weight one (i.e. edges intersect only transversally, never overlapping in segments). If overlapping edges are allowed and counted with multiplicity, the structure is called a geodesic multinet.

Prove or disprove the following two statements:

(1) For all sufficiently small nonzero ϕ ∈ (−ε, ε), the finite sequence ϕ_0(ϕ), ϕ_1(ϕ), …, ϕ_n(ϕ) consists of pairwise distinct values.

(2) Whenever (1) holds, G_n(ϕ) is a genuine geodesic net (not merely a geodesic multinet) such that every edge has weight one, G_n(ϕ) has exactly 14 unbalanced vertices, and by choosing n large one can make the number of balanced vertices of G_n(ϕ) arbitrarily large.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture concerning the finite sevenfold star construction G_n(ϕ) and the non-repetition of its suspension angles appears to remain open. Recent work (2024–2025) on geodesic nets with few boundary vertices addresses related questions, including constructions with four boundary vertices and many balanced vertices, but does not resolve this specific conjecture about the 14-boundary-vertex sevenfold star construction.

status_evidence.title: Towards Constructing Geodesic Nets with Four Boundary Vertices and an Increasing Number of Balanced Vertices
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs geodesic nets with 4 boundary vertices and up to 25 balanced vertices; mentions Gromov's question on bounding balanced vertices by unbalanced ones.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work tackles related constructions with 4 boundary vertices but does not address the 14-unbalanced-vertex sevenfold star conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Geodesic Nets: Some Examples and Open Problems
